analyzed_vuln.description: TextBasedProtocolMessage::parseFields() tracks curOffset as a signed int even though m_DataLen and HeaderField::getFieldSize() are size_t. For a very large text-protocol layer, the size_t sum can satisfy the loop bound, but `curOffset += curField->getFieldSize()` narrows/wraps it to a negative int. The wrapped offset is then passed to HeaderField. At the crash, HeaderField computes `m_DataLen - (size_t)m_NameOffsetInMessage`; converting the negative offset to size_t underflows the length to a huge value, so memchr reads outside the packet. parseFields is the root caller because it fails to preserve and validate the offset before constructing the next HeaderField.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A crafted pcap must yield an abnormally large UDP payload on a SIP source/destination port, with payload bytes recognized as a SIP request method (the PoV uses `UPDATE`). The SIP first line and subsequent text field data must make the cumulative field offset cross the range of int while the corresponding size_t offset is still below m_DataLen. The harness loads the pcap into Packet, IPv4/UDP parsing selects SipRequestLayer, its constructor calls parseFields(), and the narrowed negative field offset causes the out-of-bounds memchr read in HeaderField::HeaderField().

args: Analyze the safest minimal fix for the signed narrowing in TextBasedProtocolMessage::parseFields() at PcapPlusPlus/Packet++/src/TextBasedProtocol.cpp lines 87-133. In particular, should curOffset become size_t with an INT_MAX guard before calling HeaderField (whose constructor takes int), and how should an invalid initial m_FieldsOffset be handled without breaking invariants such as m_LastField? Are there existing project conventions for oversized offsets?

The sanitizer crash occurs when parseFields keeps a signed int curOffset while HeaderField::getFieldSize() and m_DataLen are size_t. The loop's mixed arithmetic can pass, then curOffset += size_t narrows to a negative int, and HeaderField uses that negative offset in pointer arithmetic and a size_t subtraction, causing an out-of-bounds memchr. I have inspected parseFields and HeaderField: parseFields constructs the first field immediately at int m_FieldsOffset, then loops; HeaderField stores offsets as int. The likely minimal root fix is to calculate all cumulative offsets in size_t and only construct another HeaderField if the next offset is both below m_DataLen and representable as int. I also want defense for a negative or out-of-range initial field offset, while preserving list/last-field state.
